**Matrix Vector Product**

Now calculate the value of the matrix product

    \[
    \begin{bmatrix}
        2 & 1 & 0 \\
        3 & 0 & 0 \\
        -1 & 1 & 4 
    \end{bmatrix} \cdot
    \begin{bmatrix}
        3\\-2\\1
    \end{bmatrix}
    \]

**A Linear Combination of Matrix Columns**

Explain in one or two sentences how your calculation from Q2 relates to the sum from Q1. 

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint

What do the columns of the matrix above look like? Can you find the vectors from Q1 among them?

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solution

This question is meant to highlight "what is going on" when we take a matrix-vector product, and hopefully clarify *why* the product is defined the way it is.

If $A$ is a matrix and $v$ is a vector, the product $A\cdot v$ always outputs a vector that is a linear combination of the columns of $A$. The coefficient associated with the $j$-th column is precisely the $j$-th element of $v$-- this is why the length of the vector $v$ must match the number of columns of $A$!

:::
